item.title: Elevator draft, agaiin: Re: Elevator draft, agaiin
item.content:encoded:
It would be good to keep in mind I'm new to the foundation and haven't made an scp yet, so take my criticism with a grain of salt, but these are all the things I noticed while reading it, in the same order as the article.

my (nitpicky) criticism
 my (nitpicky) criticism

I don't get why it would be esoteric? seems like it would be safe, because they can just keep it in one place, no one else has access.

If the O-5 want people to give sightings of Dr. Spencer why would they cover his eyes? I would find a different image if you can't fully show that one.

The forewords are a bit confusing, I didn't immediately know you were talking about the d class, so some disambiguation about that would be good.

Another thing about Test 1 is Dr. Spencer seems oddly unclinical, his words themselves make grammatical sense but it definitely doesn't seem clinical. He should be stating things more factually, instead of words like "hey", "you're welcome", or "lots". It just seems like he should be less replying to the D class, and more telling him what to do in a stricter way.

The diary seems good to me, clinical tone isn't required obviously, but it does seem a bit hamfisted at the end there when he mentions the scp and how he wants to use it all in one sentence at the end.

I thought Test 2 was nice, but it felt a bit forced when you said "Always talked about the 1969 Moon landing". And again, I don't really think a doctor should be saying "hey" during procedure.

The second diary entry seemed better, because it was already established that he wanted to use the elevator, so I don't think a change needs to be present in my opinion.

I like that in the 3rd test, you specify that you're talking about the D-class this time, but I'm not sure why it didn't happen before. The Foreword of this is by far the best of the 3, it doesn't feel especially forced and gives a nice overview of the D class. The test itself seemed fine, but again, Dr. Spencer seems way too non-clinical. Also I don't think there's such a thing as Kauai Beach. Kauai is an Island in Hawaii, but I may be wrong on there being no beach.

Final diary is alright, but I'm confused how he managed to nab 2 pills of scp-500, as those are under super strict lockdown with weight sensors. I also thought the reference to 939 was forced, and there wasn't any mention of him working anywhere near those before.

Overall, the most glaring issues were it being esoteric, the test logs being non-clinical and there were a lot of things that came out of nowhere, like the 939 reference, the moon landing bit, or the sudden diary entry saying he wanted to use the elevator.

Although it might sound like I don't like it, I think this is actually a pretty solid idea, and one that could work really well. As was said in previous thread's criticism, there are other transportation scps, but I can't remember any very similar to this. I would also add a bit more to the description, like if they can interact with the other people there (if any), and if they can, what it looks like to the people in those locations when the elevator comes in (this could be determined by having someone go, finding out their favorite location, sending people to that area, then sending them again).

item.title: SCP Mermaids of the Midnight Zone: Re: SCP Mermaids of the Midnight Zone
item.content:encoded:
Was asked to take a look at this. I've got a kind of list of items I want to go over, moving from small to big, if you'll bear with me.

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-X instances are believed to operate globally.

This seems unlikely to me. How does this thing adapt to different sections of the oceans like that?

In addition, all possess an exceptionally long illicium capable of extending at least 100m, and terminating into a realistic and anatomically accurate body of a human female, connected at the base of the skull.

These human lures act as a direct extension of SCP-X, showing them to possess corresponding intellect and the ability to speak.

Honestly, I'd prefer if the process here were a little more imperfect, like the lure has the general shape of a woman but in daylight it's obviously some kind of growth, or their capacity for speak and intellect is rudimentary at best. It just kinda grounds the idea, I think.

Due to SCP-X’s anomalous abilities, all tank maintenance, feedings, tests, and interviews are to be conducted solely by biologically female staff.
…
These effects are greatly amplified in biologically male individuals.

I do not think the phrase "biologically female/male" in an SCP has ever resulted in anything good. The fixation on biology isn't particularly necessary in the context of what you're doing, anyways, and adding a compulsive effect to amplify victim's desire to have sex with the fish comes with its own host of problems.

Yes, we were attacked by a madman at knifepoint.

This whole thing is a significant amount of information pushed into a small space — why not create an addendum separate from the description to convey this in a more natural manner?

Overall it's got the general shape of an article that I'd like — it's short and it's got a little twist of expectations at the end — but I feel like the way you're communicating that twist lacks a level of nuance. Having the fish state their motivations is a bit of an anticlimax. In addition I can't really develop sympathy for the SCP since I get its motivations, but it's still manufacturing victims' desire to breed and overriding their consent. I feel like you're trying to get me to realize that these fish are just lonely but I'm not convinced.

item.title: The Abyss is Safe, Looking For Co-Authors: Re: The Safe, Dark Deep
item.content:encoded:
Overall, I'm a big fan of the way the article and story is presented. I like the way the logs record the slow degradation of the mental state of the team, and the eventual total breakdown of order. While it's nothing too original, it contains a pretty interesting narrative and SCP.

+ Some Crit
- Hide Crit

SCP-XXXX holds two main anomalous properties.

This sentence and the use of "Firstly" and "Secondly" is a bit extraneous. I don't really see a need to state that their are two main anomalous properties when we are about to read them.

Hume readings in the area are incredibly low, indicating some force inside the cavern is altering reality. The side effects of this property make it so that conventional methods of terminating living organisms do not work (for reference please see Dr. Anna Lang’s research and SCP-3001).

SCP-3001 is my personal favorite, so I'm glad to see it being referenced here. However, one of the major effects of low hume levels as presented in that article is that they cause the disintegration of physical matter over time. This isn't too much of a problem, since the cave's regenerative factors likely make up for this, but it might needed to be directly stated in the article if that's the case.

There are a pretty large amount of grammatical errors in the description and some in the logs. I just suggest giving these another once-over for errors.

Also, having read the Idea thread, I personally prefer "The Abyss is Safe" for the title. It sounds a bit more original and eye catching to me.
